_context: Diagnosis workflow wf_fac9fc07-8e2 (4 Nov ~02:40 EST): finding, adversarial verdict, and the planned fix F2 that rf_ep8_ds implements. Local file paths inside refer to the author's machine and Babel.

finding.object: right hand on beige_cup (also the cup's twist track)
finding.frames: f46-51 (blend-in at lift-off), f58-68, f128-154, f176-181 (blend-out at set-down)
finding.observation: The cup's FoundationPose track spins about its own (near-symmetric) axis: -126 deg over f58-68 and -80 deg over f128-154. The real hand does not: the raw HaMeR wrist rotates +0.7 and +6.2 deg about that axis over the same frames. That makes it noise, impossible under a rigid grasp. attach_hands then rides the hand rigidly on the cup, with the grip taken at the closest frame k=f77, which comes after the first spin. As a result the reference hand must orbit the cup with no matching cup motion: +100 deg in 6 frames at lift-off (f46-51) and +73 deg at set-down (f176-181). Between those it spins with the cup at up to 27 deg/frame. Over f47-61 the reference hand sits on the wrong side of the cup, up to 138 deg and 18.4 cm from the video hand. That is past the 0.15 m wrist-termination distance, so a policy that holds the cup the way the video hand does gets terminated. A policy that follows the reference must orbit the cup while lifting it. Both failing seeds lose the cup in exactly this window. The lucky seed survives with ADD peaks at the spins.
finding.evidence:
Video crops with the reference hand (red) vs the raw HaMeR hand (yellow) and the cup axis: C:\v2d_demo\diag\ep8_handsB\hb_twist_sheet.jpg.
Hand vs cup twist: hb_twist.json and s14.out.
- bundle_merged, cup twist / raw wrist about the cup axis: f58-68 -125.7 / +0.7 deg; f128-154 -79.7 / +6.2 deg; cumulative f32-200 -145 / +28.7 deg.
- Cleaned (reference) wrist about the cup axis: +100.6 deg over f44-53 while the cup turns -1.0; +73.1 deg over f174-183 while the cup turns -1.6.
- Attached vs raw hand: up to 138 deg (f59) and 18.4 cm (f57-58); 65-80 deg and about 10 cm over f146-176.
- Fraction of projected joints inside the dilated SAM right-hand mask, attached vs raw: 0.12 vs 0.37 (f46-52), 0.48 vs 0.71 (f60-68), 0.56 vs 0.69 (f128-154).
Robot wrist reference (parquet), hb_main.json and s13.out: rotation steps 17.9-19.8 deg/frame at f46-51 (1.7-4.4 before), 22.6-27.1 at f62-65, 12.3-12.8 at f176-181; translation steps 2.1-4.46 cm/frame at f46-51 (0.4-0.8 before).
Grip frame k=77 and the rigid-ride plus 5-frame blend logic: ~/v2d_ops/kenc/hand6/ep25/code/run_load_retarget.py attach_hands (lines 620-711); report attached_0 right f46-181.
Rollouts (s13.out):
- Submitted: cup ADD rises from 1.96 to 4.93 cm over f62-65, orientation error peaks at 18.7 deg (f65), ADD 3.8 cm at f133.
- s42/s43: cup pos err > 10 cm from f50 and orientation > 0.5 rad from f54.
Training terminations: object 0.10 m / 0.50 rad, non-symmetric geodesic (lifecycle/termination.py); wrist position 0.15 m.
finding.confidence: high that this is an artefact (video, HaMeR and physics agree); medium that it is the main seed-failure cause, since the floating cup (B1) also acts at the same lift
fix_options: Twist-from-hand rule for the held, axially symmetric cup (the analogue of the spoon roll-from-wrist rule): during the right-hand hold (f45-185) replace the cup's rotation about its own axis with the raw HaMeR wrist's rotation about that axis, keeping FoundationPose position and axis direction. Then re-run attach_hands, which becomes a position-only correction. This removes the +100 deg blend-in, the -126/-80 deg spins and the +73 deg blend-out. It does not change the cup's scored error if the GT cup is axially symmetric (likely).

attach_hands guard: take the grip at the first held frame instead of the closest frame, and refuse or limit blends whose hand-to-object relative rotation exceeds about 20 deg. On its own this moves the jump to the set-down, so combine it with the twist rule.
Retrain with at least 3 seeds together with B1; expect fewer failed lifts (2/4 control seeds lost the cup at f50-54) and lower ADD peaks at f62-65 and f133.

verdict.reason:
The mechanism holds, but the score cost and the claim that it causes the failed seeds are overstated. Evidence is in C:\v2d_demo\diag\ep8_skB2\ (skb2.py, skb2.json, s1.out, skb2_markers.jpg), mirrored on Babel at ~/v2d_ops/kenc/diag/ep8_skB2/. I ran one CPU step and used no GPUs.

CONFIRMED
(1) The cup's twist is not real.
- f58-68: the cup turns -125.7 deg about its axis while the raw HaMeR wrist turns +0.7.
- f128-154: -79.7 vs +6.2.
- In hb_twist_sheet.jpg the real hand stays on the same side of the cup through both pours.
- Likely cause, from my marker overlay (skb2_markers.jpg): the mesh has 4 marker bumps about 90 deg apart (azimuths 0, -82, -180, +93 deg). Projected markers still land near the real ones at reference twists of -1 (f40), -70 (f110) and -148 (f165-184), so the twist is aliased and FoundationPose cannot pin it down.

(2) The attach mechanism works as described.
- The grip is taken after spin 1. Attached-vs-raw angle is smallest at f73 (2.1 deg) and stays at or below 3.7 deg over f68-78. The report gives a grip distance of 4.1 cm, not the finding's 3.07, so k is somewhere in f68-78, not exactly 77.
- Reference wrist rotation steps: 17.9-19.8 deg/frame at f46-51 and 12.3-12.8 at f176-181. Translation steps: 2.1-4.46 cm/frame at f46-51.
- Termination thresholds confirmed in flash_chord lifecycle/termination.py lines 43-49: wrist 0.15 m; object 0.10 m and 0.5 rad, non-symmetric.

OVERSTATED
(a) The submitted rollout loses almost nothing to the spin itself.
- A Kaggle-style twist-invariant ADD (as in AUC.py, 360 steps about the axis) equals plain ADD: cup AUC 0.8037 both ways. The rollout's own twist error stays at or below 17.5 deg, and every error in the B2 windows is position lag (position error is about equal to ADD).
- The f62-68 peak (ADD 4.95 cm at f65, position error 5.08 cm) coincides with spin 1, but also with the pour tilt from 47 to 100 deg.
- The f131-134 peak (about 3.4 cm) is the start of the second pour, before spin 2. Spin 2 itself (f137-150, about -84 deg) is tracked at 0.46-1.55 cm.
- Blend-in f46-51 has ADD 1.07-2.53 cm. Blend-out f176-181 has 0.5-0.6 cm and loses no AUC.
- Cup AUC lost across all B2 windows is 0.041, i.e. 0.020 episode AUC as an upper bound. The excess over the mid-hold loss rate is about 0.011 episode AUC, and part of that is the fast pours.

(b) "Both failing seeds lose the cup in exactly this window" is wrong.
- s42 and s43 never lifted the cup. Cup rise over f30-70 was at most 0.4 cm in s42. In s43 it was at most 1.6 cm, then the cup was knocked over and was on the floor by f80.
- Their position error passes 10 cm at f50 only because the reference rises (+6.2 cm at f50, on top of the 4.6-5 cm float).
- The successful rollouts lift the cup at f40-45, before the orbit starts (blend weight is 1/6 at f46). So the failing seeds missed the grasp at f40-46, which is confounded with B1: the float already uses about 5 of the 10 cm object-termination margin.
- Both failing seeds were already off on the pot at f3-6 (orientation error 18-25 deg, before any hand label), so they are generally weak policies.
- s44 lifted the cup and carried it through every B2 window with no B2-specific peak. It failed at f2-9 (the cup was thrown right after the f0 drop, a B1 effect) and when the cup fell off the table at the end.
- So B2 as a cause of seed failure is plausible but not shown. Over f54-61 the 0.15 m wrist limit and the 0.5 rad non-symmetric object limit cannot both be met with a natural grasp.
verdict.corrected:
IMPACT
- On the submitted rollout already in the baseline: 0, because the fix needs a retrain.
- After a retrain with a successful seed: about 0.005-0.011 episode AUC directly, not 0.03. The upper bound is 0.020, the case where every B2-window loss disappears.
- Any larger gain would have to come from a higher seed-success rate. That is unproven and confounded with B1.

CORRECTED FRAMES AND NUMBERS
- Reference hand more than 90 deg off-side: f51-62. It is 35-89 deg at f47-50.
- Wrist more than 15 cm from the HaMeR hand: f54-61 only.
- 65-80 deg and about 10 cm off: f148-176, not from f146.
- Grip frame k: somewhere in f68-78 (smallest angle at f73), not exactly 77.
- Rollout ADD peaks:
  - f63-68: 3-5 cm position lag during spin 1 and the pour tilt.
  - f131-134: start of the second pour, not spin 2.
- Failing seeds s42/s43 missed the grasp at f40-46; they did not lose a cup they were holding.

FIX
- For an axially symmetric held cup, set the cup's twist rate to zero during the hold, keeping the FoundationPose axis direction and position, then re-run attach_hands. Prefer this over copying HaMeR's twist: the HaMeR wrist rotates 75-239 deg in total over these windows, i.e. jitter.
- Retrain with at least 3 seeds, preferably together with B1. Keep the submitted 0.897 own-ref rollout unless a new seed beats it on own-ref.

CAVEAT
- If the organisers did not mark the cup as symmetric (it carries 4 Vicon markers), the reference's -148 deg twist at the end (the hand suggests about +29) would be a large reconstruction loss, and the fix would matter far more. This cannot be checked.

planned_fix_F2.name: F2 despin the held symmetric cup, then re-attach the right hand spin-free (sym_common 'despin'), rebuilt from the base's exact merged bundle, with F1 on top
planned_fix_F2.fix_type: roll de-noising by rule plus a hand attach re-run (CPU scene rebuild)
planned_fix_F2.automatic_rule: Applies to objects the kit README lists as axially symmetric (beige_cup, blue_cup; axial spin is unscored). Replace the object's rotation about its mesh symmetry axis (the PCA axis through the surface centroid) with frame 0's: T'[t] = T[t]·S(-theta_t), where theta_t is the twist of R0^T Rt about that axis. Position, axis direction and the axis line are unchanged. Then attach the holding hand spin-free: the hand rides the cup's translation and tilt, the grip is still taken at the closest frame, and the blends use the continuous rotation branch. No per-episode numbers.

planned_fix_F2.risk:
The direct gain is small: 0.005-0.011 per the B2 verdict, 0.020 upper bound. Any larger gain would come from a higher seed success rate, which is plausible but unproven and confounded with F1.

The rebuilt parquet differs from bob1's only in three ways: the cup twist, the right-hand reference over f44-200, and about 0.3% contact-label noise.

If the organisers did not mark the beige cup as symmetric, the twist becomes scored. It would move toward the hand-consistent value; the base ends -160 deg vs f0.

Plain own-ref is not comparable with bob1's; use spin-invariant own-ref (~/v2d_ops/kenc/hand5/ep10/sym_ownref.py).

Alternative arm: patch_respinf.py, the ep10-proven rule (+0.031, 3/3 seeds), should behave almost the same here. The video wrist barely turns about the cup: +0.7 and +6.2 deg in the spin windows.
